title: U.S. House · California's 6th District
area: Covers part of the Sacramento metropolitan area, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.
Ballotpedia lists incumbent Kevin Kiley's party affiliation for this election as 'No party preference'; he was previously elected to the U.S. House as a Republican.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Kevin Kiley placed first with 24.3% (47,165 votes) and Richard Pan (D) placed second with 23.2% (45,008 votes), narrowly ahead of Republican Michael Stansfield's 20.1%, out of 194,217 total votes cast.

candidates.name: Kevin Kiley
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Kevin Kiley is a lawyer and former teacher who served in the California State Assembly from 2016 to 2022 and has represented California in the U.S. House since 2023. He was elected as a Republican and in March 2026 announced he was leaving the party to serve as an independent, though he still caucuses with Republicans. After Proposition 50 redrew the state's districts, he is running in the 6th District.

background.text: According to his official biography, he is the son of a special education teacher, grew up in the district and graduated from Granite Bay High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard University in 2007, a master's in secondary education from Loyola Marymount University in 2009, and a law degree from Yale Law School in 2012.

Began his career as a 10th-grade English teacher at Manual Arts High School in Los Angeles, where, according to his official biography, he chaired the English Department and founded a speech and debate team.

After law school he worked as a lawyer, including on the civil case against Huawei Technologies over intellectual property theft, and later became a California Deputy Attorney General; Ballotpedia also lists adjunct professor among his past roles.
Was first elected to the California State Assembly in 2016 and served until his election to Congress in 2022, representing Assembly District 6.

Elected to the U.S. House in 2022 to represent the 3rd District and took office January 3, 2023. He serves on the Judiciary, Education and Workforce, and Transportation and Infrastructure committees and chairs the Education and Workforce Subcommittee on Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education.
His official biography says he introduced the PRESS Act, which passed the House with bipartisan support, and co-chairs the Inventions Caucus.

On March 9, 2026, he announced he was dropping his Republican affiliation and would serve as an independent, while continuing to caucus with Republicans to keep his committee assignments; the Associated Press reported he chose to run in the 6th District rather than against Rep. Tom McClintock after the state's boundaries were redrawn.
According to his official biography, he and his wife, Chelsee, reside in Rocklin.

priorities.text: Chairs the House Subcommittee on Early Childhood, Elementary, and Secondary Education and says he fought for $5 billion in education dollars for low- and middle-income families to access services like special education, tuition and tutoring.

Says protecting access to Head Start early-childhood education, health, nutrition and family-support services is important, citing his role as chairman of the education subcommittee that oversees the program.

positions.summary: Supports the federal Education Freedom Tax Credit, which gives taxpayers a credit for donations to scholarship-granting organizations that fund families' education expenses, and has publicly called on California to participate.
positions.quote: Last year, I fought for $5 billion in education dollars for low and middle-income families to access services like special education, tuition, and tutoring.

positions.summary: Introduced bipartisan legislation with Rep. Sam Liccardo to extend the expiring Affordable Care Act subsidies; CalMatters reports he also supports the Medicaid work requirements enacted in H.R. 1.
positions.quote: I introduced the Fix It Act with Sam Liccardo, bipartisan legislation to extend these expiring Affordable Care Act subsidies.

positions.summary: Says he voted to disapprove the tariffs on Canada and to reclaim Congress's authority over tariffs because tariffs have raised the cost of living.
positions.quote: I voted to disapprove the tariffs for Canada because I think tariffs have raised the cost of living.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, chairing its Workforce Protections Subcommittee, during the 2023-2024 session.
Served on the House Committee on the Judiciary and the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure during the 2023-2024 session.

candidates.name: Richard Pan
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Physician; former California State Senator, District 6 (2014-2022)

summary.text: Richard Pan is a pediatrician and former UC Davis faculty member who served in the California State Assembly from 2010 to 2014 and the State Senate from 2014 to 2022, where he chaired the Senate Health Committee. His campaign website says he authored legislation to raise school vaccination rates after the 2015 Disneyland measles outbreak. He is running as a Democrat on a platform of protecting health care and basing federal policy on science.

background.text: Describes himself as the son of Taiwanese immigrants who received a good public school education.
Earned a B.S. from Johns Hopkins University, an M.A. in public health from Harvard University, and an M.D. from the University of Pittsburgh.
Worked as a physician at UC Davis Children's Hospital and as an associate professor of pediatrics at UC Davis; according to his campaign website, he led UC Davis' Pediatric Residency Program.

According to his campaign website, he founded Communities and Physicians Together, a program partnering pediatricians with neighborhoods, and co-founded 'Healthy Kids Healthy Future,' which it says provided health, dental and vision coverage to over 65,000 children in the Sacramento region.
Elected to the California State Assembly in 2010 and served in District 9 until 2014.
Elected to the California State Senate in 2014 and represented District 6 until 2022; he chaired the Senate Health Committee and Public Employment and Retirement Committee.

His campaign website says TIME magazine named him a 'hero' for legislation to increase school vaccination rates after the 2015 Disneyland measles outbreak, and that he authored state laws on pre-existing conditions, youth sports smoking bans and prescription drug costs.
Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, finishing second behind Kiley, to the general election in the 6th District.

priorities.text: Campaign describes him as a public health advocate running to oppose Trump administration and Robert F. Kennedy Jr. policies on healthcare and science.
priorities.quote: Dr. Pan is running for Congress to fight Trump and Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s attack on healthcare and science.

positions.summary: Campaign site says that in Congress he will stop the administration from gutting the Affordable Care Act and will protect Medicare.
positions.quote: In Congress, Dr. Pan will stop Trump from gutting the Affordable Care Act, protect Medicare, stop insurance companies from denying critical care prescribed by doctors, and fight to lower prescription drug costs.

positions.summary: Voted yes on AB 1482 (the Tenant Protection Act, capping annual rent increases statewide), which passed the California Senate 25-10 on 2019-09-10.
Voted yes on SB 35 (streamlining local approval of affordable housing developments that meet zoning and labor standards), which passed the California Senate 25-12 on 2017-06-01.
Campaign site says that in Congress he will work to institute universal background checks and a ban on assault weapons.
positions.quote: In Congress he’ll work to institute universal background checks and a ban on assault weapons.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he protected abortion rights after Roe v. Wade was overturned and will work to codify Roe in Congress.
positions.quote: In Congress he will work to codify Roe.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will fight to roll back the President's tariffs, which he says are raising prices.
positions.quote: fight to roll back Trump's tariff taxes that are raising prices on Californians

positions.summary: Campaign site says he believes ICE must be overhauled and replaced with an agency that enforces the law fairly, and that he will fight for a path to citizenship.
positions.quote: Dr. Pan believes Trump's ICE must be overhauled and replaced with an agency that doesn't kill Americans and separate families, enforces the law fairly, and protects people's constitutional rights.

record.text: Chaired the California Senate Health Committee during the 2019-2020 and 2021-2022 sessions.
As a state senator, authored California's law tightening childhood vaccination exemption requirements, according to his campaign.
Voted yes on AB 1482 (the Tenant Protection Act of 2019, capping annual rent increases statewide), which passed the California Senate 25-10 on 2019-09-10.
Voted yes on SB 35 (streamlining local approval of affordable housing developments that meet zoning and labor standards), which passed the California Senate 25-12 on 2017-06-01.

researchNotes: Kevin Kiley has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and his site (kiley.house.gov) no longer has a dedicated Issues page; his stated priorities and positions above are drawn from recent posts on his official site, which is the fuller record available. Pan's vaccine-law authorship claim is from his own campaign site and was not independently verified against a bill record. Biography gaps: Pan's birthplace and birth year and Kiley's birth year are not documented in loaded sources; the 2021 Newsom recall claim in Kiley's earlier summary was removed because no loaded source shows him as a recall candidate.
